content:
cs-jordan: FYI — multiple customers reporting 503s from hosted inference starting ~2026-03-17T22:21Z UTC. CS saw a spike ~1200/s, main report from Acme (prod).

sre-raj: Investigating now. Any sample request ids or patterns?

cs-jordan: Sample request_id req_0a9f12 attached in ticket. Happens during toolcall/stream with large context. Customer says it times out then client gets 503.

eng-amy: I pulled k8s events — affected worker pods on node gpu-3 restarted repeatedly. Status shows CrashLoopBackOff -> OOMKilled -> exit code 137.

ops-bot: [automated] node gpu-3 nvml event: GPU_MEMORY_ERROR at 2026-03-17T22:21:57Z.

eng-mike: Logs from pod req_0a9f12:
```
CUDA out of memory: Tried to allocate 5.12 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total)
#0  0x7f... attention_kernel.cu:412
#1  0x7f... infer_runtime.cpp:1289
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
```

eng-amy: Looks like prefetch + dynamic batching pushed a single allocation over the limit. Toolcall path is prefetch-heavy and context_size for that request was ~62k tokens.

sre-raj: Can we reproduce locally with that request payload? If so capture core and nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY output.

eng-mike: Reproduced with stress script (uses sample payload). Repro cmd:
```
PREFETCH=1 BATCH_MAX=1024 ./scripts/repro_toolcall.sh --context 62000 --tools 8
```
This triggers same OOM and segfault in attention kernel. Collected gdb backtrace.

eng-amy: Short-term mitigation: disable prefetch for this model variant and route matching requests to a prefetch-disabled variant. I'll create a routing rule to divert requests with param X-toolcall=true.

eng-mike: Implemented routing mask and updated canary at 22:28 UTC. Also enabled CPU fallback for any failed GPU allocations for that customer route.

cs-jordan: Error rate dropped — from ~1200/s 503s down to ~80/s within ~3 minutes after the routing change. Customer confirmed degraded responses are flowing. :relieved:

eng-mike: For postmortem we need: core dump, nvml and driver logs, pod yaml, and kv-cache stats. I saved core to /var/dumps/infer-20260317-22-22-core.gz and uploaded nvml dump to s3://incidents/INC-20260317/nvml_dump.tgz. Ticket INC-20260317 created.

sre-raj: Good. Root cause looks like an interaction: dynamic batch growth + aggressive kv-prefetching with large context triggered transient overcommit of GPU memory, followed by bad kernel path that didn't gracefully OOM. We'll add an allocator guard in runtime to pre-check prefetch budget.

eng-amy: Working on patch: guard prefetch by current_batch_memory + prefetch_estimate <= gpu_budget. Will open PR with tests and a feature flag (runtime.prefetch_guard=true).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of runtime-prefetch-guard -> model/x-7b prefetched-canary at 22:47 UTC succeeded for 5 pods.

eng-amy: Canary running for ~30m, no OOMs on canary pods. Plan to roll to remaining pods in low-risk wave tomorrow 02:00 UTC if telemetry stays green.

cs-jordan: Customer asked for RCA + ETA. I'll draft a customer note linking the mitigation and ETA.

sre-raj: Post-incident action items: (1) add prefetch memory accounting (2) add route-based rate limiter for heavy-toolcall paths (3) add alert for repeated OOMKilled on same node within 5m.

eng-mike: Added repro script and logs to the ticket. Also note: core shows segfault during kernel launch surface — file uploaded.

cs-jordan: Thanks team — closing loop with Acme and leaving this thread open until patch is fully rolled.
